Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National New presidential jet purchase was driven by cost concerns, not improved economy – Kwakye Ofosu Source : Emma Ankrah 17 November 2026 8:17pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has rejected suggestions that the purchase of the new presidential jet was justified by an improvement in the country's economic circumstances.
According to him, the decision to procure a new presidential aircraft was driven by concerns over the cost of maintaining the existing Falcon 900 and the expense of chartering private jets, not an improvement in the economy.
Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Top Story on Tuesday, November 17, he said the Ghana Air Force had made an urgent request to government for new aircraft following the August 6 disaster, citing frequent breakdowns of its fleet and difficulties obtaining spare parts.
Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the Air Force had presented a Cabinet memorandum recommending the purchase of four military transport helicopters and two executive jets.
He said the Falcon 900 had become economically unsustainable as the primary aircraft for presidential travel because of its frequent breakdowns and high maintenance costs.
“Nobody has said that we are going to buy a jet because the economy has improved...They were clear that given the frequent breakdowns of the Falcon 900, it had become economically unsustainable to maintain it as the primary aircraft of presidential travel because overall it costs more to maintain, and its absence also occasioned risks, where a president opts to charter a private jet,” he said.
Mr Kwakye Ofosu argued that when the cost of maintaining the aircraft and chartering private jets was considered, it exceeded the cost of procuring a replacement.
He said government decided to purchase the four military helicopters and only one executive jet, rather than the two recommended by the Air Force.
“The government took the decision that we will purchase the four military helicopters and then one executive jet, which is the smaller one they recommended,” he said.
Mr Kwakye Ofosu said Parliament approved the procurement on December 4, 2025, after the then Acting Minister of Defence and the Minister of Finance presented the request.
He disclosed that the first military helicopter had arrived earlier in the year, while the new Falcon 6X arrived on Monday, November 16.
According to him, a second military helicopter was expected within the following two weeks, with two more to complete the Air Force’s requested fleet.
While rejecting suggestions that the purchase was justified by an improvement in the country's economic circumstances, he, however, pointed to changes in the country's debt position, saying the previous government had declared that Ghana was unable to meet its debt obligations and had left bondholders without coupon payments for several months.
He said the current government was now making bond payments ahead of schedule, which he cited as evidence of an improvement in the economy.
His comments follow criticism from the Minority over the government's decision to acquire a new presidential aircraft, with members questioning the need for the purchase amid the country's economic challenges.

The debate has also revived comments by the Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, who, while the NDC was in opposition, argued that Ghana could not afford a new presidential jet given the country's economic circumstances.
